title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance, and Manager Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard practices for hiring, candidate experience SLAs, new hire onboarding, the performance and feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, people-ops partners, and people managers. Follow these procedures to ensure consistent candidate and employee experiences, predictable hiring economics, and high-quality people decisions.

Key goals
- Reduce time-to-offer while maintaining interview quality: target time-to-offer = 21 calendar days for engineering roles.
- Deliver consistent onboarding that enables new hires to reach independent contribution within 90 days.
- Run objective performance cycles with regular feedback and quarterly calibration.
- Equip managers with templates, timelines, and ownership checklists to reduce variance.

Ownership and escalation
- People Ops (hiring@redwood.com): owner of process, templates, and compliance.
- Recruiter (assigned per req): candidate sourcing, scheduling, offer logistics.
- Hiring Manager: role definition, interview team, role decision.
- Interviewers / Panel: apply rubric, document feedback.
- Escalations: first to People Ops lead; if unresolved, escalate to Head of People.

Hiring process (standard req flow)
1) Create req and intake (Hiring manager + Recruiter)
   - Use the standard job description template. Attach must-have vs nice-to-have skills.
   - Timeline: intake completed within 3 business days.
2) Sourcing and first contact (Recruiter)
   - Initial candidate outreach window: 7-14 days. Recruiter responds to inbound applicants within 48 business hours.
3) Screen (phone or short video, 30 min)
   - Conducted by recruiter or hiring manager. Confirm salary band, work authorization, eligibility, base qualifications.
4) Technical/functional interviews (2-4 rounds typically)
   - Structure: 1 take-home exercise (optional for mid/senior infra roles) + 2 live interviews focusing on system design / role-specific skills + 1 culture / collaboration interview.
5) Debrief and decision (Hiring manager + interviewers + recruiter)
   - Decision target: within 3 business days after final interview. Use the interview rubric (see section below).
6) Offer and negotiation (Recruiter + Finance for comp approval)
   - Offer letter template is required. Recruiter gets written comp sign-off before verbal offer.
7) Background checks and references (People Ops)
   - Start reference checks after verbal offer accepted; complete before start date when possible.

Interview rubric and feedback expectations
- Provide written feedback in Greenhouse within 48 hours after interview. Feedback should include:
  - Competency scores (0-4) on: role skills, problem solving, communication, collaboration, ownership.
  - Written examples: 1-2 concrete observations.
  - Hire/No-hire recommendation and rationale.
- Use objective evidence: code samples, tradeoffs discussed, postmortems referenced, design diagrams.
- Panel calibration: for senior hires, schedule a 30-min calibration call before extending an offer if panel opinions vary.

Candidate experience SLAs (targets)
- Recruiter response to inbound applicant: 48 business hours.
- Screen scheduled within 7 business days.
- Loop completion (from first interview to final decision): median 14 calendar days. Target: <= 21 days.
- Candidate NPS target after process: >= 70.

Diversity, equity & inclusion (DEI) requirements
- All roles must include at least one diverse slate goal during sourcing (gender/race/experience where applicable).
- Interview panels for senior roles should include at least one interviewer from outside the hiring team for calibration and perspective.

Offer & compensation process
- Managers propose band & level. Recruiter confirms market data and total comp with People Ops and Finance.
- Approval matrix: Recruiter -> Head of People (if above band midpoint by >15%) -> CFO (if equity or special comp exceptions required).
- Standard offer includes base, equity range, target bonus (if applicable), and notice of benefits start date.

Onboarding (First 90 days)
Overview: a consistent onboarding plan reduces time-to-productivity. People Ops provides an onboarding coordinator for all new hires in Departments above 5 people.
Pre-Start (1-2 weeks before start)
- People Ops: send welcome packet, benefits enrollment info, calendar invites for Day 1 orientation.
- IT: provision laptop, grant base cloud accounts, Slack, Google Workspace, and internal VPN access.
- Manager: share Team Overview, 30/60/90 plan, and first-week agenda.
Day 1\- Orientation (People Ops): 2-hour session covering company mission, security baseline, payroll, and benefits.
- Team welcome: 1-hour team intro and workspace setup.
Week 1 checklist (Manager + New hire)\- Goals: complete HR paperwork, meet core stakeholders, set initial OKRs, and install dev environment.
- 1:1 scheduled weekly with manager.
30-day milestones\- Complete role-specific training modules.
- Deliver first small deliverable (bugfix, document, experiment).
- Manager assesses ramp progress and documents in the onboarding tracker.
60-day milestones\- Contributes to team projects with reduced supervision.
- Begins owning a small component/feature.
90-day milestones (end of probation)\- Demonstrates consistent delivery and communication.
- Formal 90-day check-in: manager + People Ops (pass/fail probation discussion).
Onboarding success metrics\- Target: 90% of hires have dev environment and access by Day 3.
- Target: 80% of hires meet their 30-day milestones.

Equipment & access checklist (example table)
| Item | Owner | Target completion |
| Laptop (MacBook Pro) | IT | Day 0-3 |
| VPN / VPC access | IT | Day 0-3 |
| GitHub team membership | Manager/Platform | Day 1 |
| Cloud IAM role | Manager/Infra | Day 3 |
| Security training signed | New hire | Day 7 |

Performance & feedback cycle
Cadence\- Continuous feedback is expected. Formal cycles are:
  - Quarterly check-ins: one-page update + 1:1 focused on goals, blockers, growth.
  - Annual performance review (calendar-year): summary ratings, calibration, and compensation changes.
  - Promotion windows: quarterly nominations with documentation.
Manager responsibilities
- Run weekly 1:1s (30-60 minutes) and document key outcomes in the manager notes template.
- Deliver regular feedback using the Situation-Behavior-Impact (SBI) model.
- Prepare and submit quarterly check-in notes 48 hours before calibration meetings.
- Coach direct reports on career paths; document progress in Career Conversation template.
Calibration and rating guidance
- Calibration committee: managers + one People Ops partner. Frequency: quarterly before compensation cycles.
- Rating scale: Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations, Needs Improvement. Managers must submit written evidence for any Exceeds Expectations or Needs Improvement ratings.
Promotions and leveling
- Promotion packet: updated resume, manager memo with 3-5 concrete examples, peer feedback, and proposed new level.
- Timeline: promotion packets reviewed within 6 weeks of submission.
- Leveling rubric: use the engineering leveling matrix (link in related_pages).
Probation, performance improvement, and offboarding
- Standard probation: 90 days for new hires; extendable by People Ops with written rationale (max 30 days).
- Performance Improvement Plan (PIP): used when consistent performance is below expectations. PIP should be timeboxed (30-90 days), include measurable objectives, owner, and People Ops oversight.
- Offboarding: Manager initiates offboarding checklist; IT and Security revoke credentials on the last working day. Exit interview is scheduled by People Ops.

Manager toolkit and templates (what to use)
- Job description template (People Ops): required for all new reqs.
- Interview scorecard (Greenhouse).
- 30/60/90 onboarding checklist (spreadsheet template).
- Manager notes and 1:1 template.
- Promotion packet template and sample memos.
- PIP template and sign-off flow.

Training and manager enablement
- Quarterly manager training covers interviewing, feedback, leveling, and inclusive hiring. Attendance is required for new managers within 60 days of promotion/hire.

Compliance and record-keeping
- Maintain candidate records in Greenhouse for 2 years to comply with audit requirements.
- Store offer letters and signed contracts in Workday.
- Background check vendor: Standard checks for criminal and employment verification; additional checks for regulated roles.

Metrics we track (people-ops dashboard)
- Time-to-fill (median days): target <= 45 days.
- Time-to-offer: target <= 21 days.
- New hire retention at 6 months: target >= 90%.
- Candidate NPS: target >= 70.
- Onboarding completion rate by Day 30: target >= 80%.
